questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Sweden?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: Sweden's capital city is Stockholm, which is also Sweden's largest city, with almost one million people.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Sweden?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: Sweden has an official majority language, Swedish (the Swedish word for the language is svenska).

questions.prompt: What money is used in Sweden?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: The currency remains the Swedish krona (Swedish crown).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Ulf Kristersson was elected Prime Minister in September _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: Ulf Kristersson was elected Prime Minister in September 2022.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Sweden became a member of the European Union (EU) on 1 January _____ and NATO on 7 March 2024.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: Sweden became a member of the European Union (EU) on 1 January 1995 and NATO on 7 March 2024.
